chunks: And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said:

I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Does the Muhrim (one in Ihram) shade himself on his mount and offer a ransom if the sun and rain harm him?' He said: 'Yes.' I asked: 'What is the ransom?' He said: 'A sheep.' And the Muhrim, if his Ihram is for the Umrah that he enjoys until the Hajj, then if he shades himself, two expiations are required for him. He narrated that.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعُ بِهَا إِلَى الْحَجِّ: He enjoys it until Hajj (Umrat al-Tamattu')

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and ransom for a Muhrim who shades themselves from sun or rain?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *kaffarah* (expiation) for breaking Ihram restrictions due to necessity, specifically shading from sun or rain. It distinguishes between a single expiation for general Ihram and a double expiation for Umrat al-Tamattu', reflecting the cumulative nature of the two pilgrimage rites. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ease (*rukhas*) with accountability in ritual purity and worship.
